analysis.one_liner: Vedanta Limited is a diversified metals and mining company that, after a 2026 demerger, now runs zinc-lead-silver (via Hindustan Zinc), copper smelting, ferrochrome and port/logistics businesses, having spun off its aluminium, oil & gas, power and iron & steel units into four separately listed companies.
analysis.whats_happening: Vedanta reported record Q2 FY27 results on 28 October 2026, its first full quarter on a post-demerger basis: revenue of ₹25,812 crore and PAT of ₹6,202 crore, up 151% YoY on a company-stated comparable basis, driven by record zinc/silver output and a 29% drop in zinc production costs. It also paid its first dividend since the June 2026 demerger (₹5/share, record date 14 October 2026), and net debt fell to just ₹3,675 crore (Net Debt/EBITDA of 0.1x), with management guiding to possible net-cash status by Q3 FY27.
analysis.plain_terms: The 'old' Vedanta was split into five companies in mid-2026: this Vedanta Limited kept zinc, copper, ferrochrome and ports, while aluminium, oil & gas, power and iron & steel became four new listed companies, with shareholders given one share in each for every Vedanta share they held. That's the main reason the stock looks like it crashed 69% from its April 2026 peak - most of that 'fall' is value that moved into the four new stocks, not value that vanished. What's left is a smaller, zinc-and-copper business that just posted record profit and is paying down debt fast, but its promoter, Vedanta Resources, still leans heavily on dividends from this company to service its own debt.
analysis.quarters: On a comparable, post-demerger restated basis, Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) revenue grew 57% YoY to ₹25,812 crore, EBITDA grew 106% YoY to ₹9,938 crore, and PAT grew 151% YoY to ₹6,202 crore. Management attributed this to record Hindustan Zinc mined (271kt, +5% YoY) and refined (264kt, +7% YoY) output, record silver production (173 tonnes, +20% YoY), a 29% YoY fall in zinc cost of production, and ramped-up copper cathode output (46kt). Some press reports quote different YoY growth (17%, 78%) depending on whether they use the old consolidated aluminium-included base or the company's own restated base - the 151%/106% figures are more meaningful since the company itself frames them as 'comparable post-demerger basis.'
analysis.performance_read: Long-run price returns for VEDL are distorted by the June 2026 demerger: shareholders received one share each of four new companies (aluminium, oil & gas, power, iron & steel) for every Vedanta share held, so the standalone VEDL price understates what a long-term holder actually has. The -51% 1-year return and the 69% drawdown from the April 2026 peak largely reflect this split rather than value destruction; the true return should be measured on the combined value of all five listings, which is Not verified here - check combined value of VEDL plus the four spin-offs on Screener. Even allowing for that, over 3 and 5 years VEDL has lagged peer Hindalco (+96% and +91% vs VEDL's +38% and +58%) and only modestly beaten the Nifty.
analysis.valuation_read: A trailing P/E near 4.7-5x and P/B near 1.8x look cheap on paper, but that is partly because Q2 FY27 profit was inflated by a cyclical upswing in zinc prices and a sharp fall in zinc costs - commodity earnings like these don't move in a straight line, so capitalising a peak-cycle quarter at a low multiple can overstate the discount. Why it looks cheap: a cyclical, cost-driven profit spike plus a market still digesting the demerger. Whether it actually is cheap depends on where zinc and copper prices settle over the next few quarters - unresolved, as shown by the stock trading just above its 52-week low of ₹225.6 despite the record quarter.
analysis.growth_read: Growth in the June quarter was both margin- and volume-led: zinc mined metal volumes rose 5% YoY and refined metal 7% YoY, silver output rose 20% YoY, and copper cathode volumes ramped up, while zinc's cost of production fell 29% YoY, widening margins on top of higher volumes. Volume up and costs down together is a healthier mix for a commodity business than margin expansion on flat volumes, though it still depends on metal prices Vedanta does not control.
analysis.health_read: Vedanta converted its record profit into real cash - net debt fell by ₹4,624 crore in a single quarter to just ₹3,675 crore, taking Net Debt/EBITDA to 0.1x, with gross debt of ₹30,297 crore against cash of ₹26,622 crore. The bigger risk sits one level up: parent Vedanta Resources has a history of pulling large dividends out of Vedanta Limited to service its own offshore debt, and the promoter group's stake remains substantially encumbered under bond covenants (₹2.13 trillion/~$25.66bn equivalent disclosed in September 2026). The operating business itself looks financially sound; the overhang is parent-level leverage and governance risk, not Vedanta Limited's own balance sheet.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 54.72% of Vedanta Limited, unchanged in the September 2026 quarter; FIIs hold 15.78% and mutual funds 5.09%. The promoter stake carries a long history of pledging/encumbrance tied to parent Vedanta Resources' debt - filings show 54.72% of shares encumbered under bond covenants dated September 2026, even as an earlier 51.93% encumbrance was released that same month following a bond repayment. In practice, the bulk of the promoter stake has stayed encumbered through one facility or another for years. No marquee independent value investor stands out on the public shareholder register in available data - Not verified, check the latest shareholding pattern on Screener for individual non-institutional holders.
strengths: Net Debt/EBITDA fell to 0.1x, with net debt down to ₹3,675 crore and management guiding toward net-cash status by Q3 FY27
Record Q2 FY27 zinc output (271kt mined, +5% YoY) alongside a 29% YoY fall in zinc cost of production
ROE around 36% and ROCE in the mid-to-high teens on the restated post-demerger base
First post-demerger dividend (₹5/share, record date 14 Oct 2026) continuing a long dividend-paying history (TTM yield ~6.7%)
watchpoints: 54.72% of the promoter's stake remains encumbered under Vedanta Resources' bond covenants as of September 2026 - a recurring governance overhang
Current profitability rides a cyclical upswing in zinc/copper prices and falling costs; a reversal in either would compress the EBITDA that debt reduction depends on
Post-demerger YoY comparisons mix restated and unrestated bases across different news reports - single headline growth percentages should be treated cautiously
The 69% drawdown from the April 2026 peak is mostly a demerger artifact (four new listings absorbed the value), not a pure loss - but the true combined return is Not verified here
analysis.one_thing: Whether the encumbrance on Vedanta Resources' 54.72% stake in Vedanta Limited keeps shrinking as bonds are repaid, or whether fresh bond issuances re-encumber the stock as fast as old ones are released - that, more than the operating numbers, will determine whether the governance overhang is actually resolving.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue/EBITDA/PAT and net debt figures were cross-checked across multiple reports (Business Standard, Investing.com, GuruFocus, Tradebrains, Kotak) and were consistent on the 'comparable post-demerger basis' framing; some outlets quoted different YoY growth (17%, 78%), likely reflecting unrestated pre-demerger comparisons, set aside in favour of the company's own restated 151%/106% figures. P/E, P/B, ROE and ROCE vary modestly by source (e.g., ROCE quoted as both 15.93% and 18.72%) - treat as approximate. Could not verify the current combined market value of VEDL plus the four 2026 spin-offs (VAML, Vedanta Oil & Gas, Vedanta Power, Vedanta Iron & Steel), so true post-demerger total shareholder return is not computed here - check on Screener. Promoter encumbrance disclosures from September 2026 are genuinely complex (simultaneous release of one tranche and creation of another) and are described qualitatively rather than reconciled to one exact figure.
